Domestic opportunities after Palace were forthcoming but Kaminski says: “The person has to match the project, and while things were coming up, I didn’t feel they were a match. When Palace came up, that was a match for me, it was almost perfect in terms of personnel, being able to build something; it was somewhere I could call home. And then my agent contacted me and a recruitment agency got involved because Brann were looking for a new head coach, and it happened really quickly.

“Sometimes you don’t really realise what is going on until 24 hours down the line, you’re moving to Norway. One minute you’re in London and 48 hours later you’re on a plane, but I snapped it up because for me to get to a WSL club fighting for a title was going to be difficult, I’m still on a journey in management but I’ve been coaching for years.”

It’s come on a lot and thankfully now we’re in a different place where we can leave that behind and reward people for their skills.”

“It was a course you couldn’t buy,” she says. “It was led by Steve Parish, a great chair, great people at the club who were able to stretch me in the role. I met fantastic people; Palace will always be my home. It’s a well-run club, but those 18 months were a crash course in how to function, especially when things aren’t going well, and things are stressful. There are things I’ve reflected on, where I think I could have controlled it better, and there’s other things [that] I think were out of my hands.”
Kaminski says “flying to games has been a huge change” in Norway, where she is enjoying “fantastic scenery” and senses a country “very proud of its football”. Her obsession with the sport remains.

“I’m constantly watching games. I was addicted to football and still am. I’ll put on a Bundesliga game and see what I would do at half-time in whatever scenario they’re in. I still have that hunger and drive as when I did all those years out in the cold and the rain in London. I was fortunate enough to work in some top clubs and with some top people. By the time I got to Palace I found it easier than I first thought, or I should say smoother.

“The coaching part of being on the ground for so many years has given me so much knowledge, developing my way of playing over and over again, and who knows, that’s just the start. It will change and evolve; we’re playing some good football here. I’ve won in England, won promotion with Tottenham and Palace, and now I want to prove I can do it abroad.”
